evidence.claim: CNAS argued in May 2026 that the defense industrial base remains shallow and fragile, with DoD visibility often lost beyond tier two and subtier suppliers exposed to uneven demand signals and appropriations.
The Serenity-relevant bottleneck is likely not just federal appropriations, but the ability of qualified contractors to turn appropriations into bonded, staffed, compliant, margin-positive projects.

memory_update.text: TPC should remain in the federal infrastructure contractor universe due to explicit Guam military and waterfront repair backlog plus cited Pacific Deterrence Initiative opportunities; key risk is project execution and margin conversion.
GVA is a mid-cap reference/underfollowed hybrid for federal heavy civil, border, and mission-critical infrastructure; validate federal CAP and revenue share in latest filings.
ORN is a small-cap underfollowed marine/port/dredging execution-capacity candidate; verify federal/public mix, vessel qualification, backlog quality, and cash conversion.
AMRC is a government-facility energy-infrastructure contractor candidate; verify federal ESPC receivables, government revenue durability, project backlog, and supplier risk.

Great Lakes Dredge & Dock was highly relevant to federal dredging and Army Corps exposure, but appears to have been acquired by Saltchuk and delisted in April 2026, so it should not be treated as a current US-listed candidate.
